pulls.title: 8397270: Gracefully shutdown poller threads at VM exit
pulls.author: AlanBateman
pulls.body_excerpt: Threads in native can delay VM termination by up to 300ms (see VM_Exit::wait_for_threads_in_native_to_block). The I/O poller mechanism that allows virtual threads to park until a file descriptor is ready for I/O requires one or more platform threads blocked in kqueue, epoll_wait etc. waiting for I/O events. These threads can delay VM shutdown when there isn't any other threads in native delaying the shutdown. The changes proposed here add a shutdown hook to wakeup the pollers at VM shutdown. It is configured to run after the application shutdown hooks have completed and before the deleteOnExit

pulls.title: 8397016: ZGC: SIGILL in barrier with -XX:-UseLSE
pulls.author: stefank
pulls.body_excerpt: `MacroAssembler::cmpxchg` clobbers `rscratch1` when we're running with -XX:-UseLSE. The problem is at `store_exclusive(rscratch1, new_val, addr, size, release);` if either of `new_val` or `addr` aliases `rscratch1`. I've added asserts that checks for this, both in `MacroAssembler::cmpxchg` and in the ZGC code, where in fact did pass in `rscratch1` in `addr`. The fix is to shuffle around our temp registers, similarly to how we have it in the C1 code. pulls.title: 8393271: VectorAPI: ByteVector argument to a non-inlined method is materialized on the heap
pulls.author: vpelikh
pulls.body_excerpt: ## Problem A Vector API value passed as an argument to a method that C2 does **not** inline is materialized on the heap at the call site. The callee is compiled separately, so the value cannot stay in a SIMD register across the boundary; C2 boxes it as a vector proxy object plus its primitive array payload. A method that applies a sequence of Vector API operations (no loops, just one operation after another) is large by construction: each operation is a separate call in the bytecode, so a method with a dozen of them easily exceeds `FreqInlineSize` (325 bytes by default). pulls.title: 8389749: RISC-V: Optimize RVV string/array comparison with tiered approach
pulls.author: zifeihan
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, please consider. The current RVV element_compare uses a single-LMUL loop for all input sizes. Since short strings dominate in practice [1], the per-iteration loop overhead is disproportionate for small inputs. This patch replaces the loop with a tiered strategy: short inputs are handled by a single vl-bounded compare (m1/m2/m4 depending on size), and long inputs use a fixed-stride m4 loop with a vl-bounded tail.
